items.title: Evaluating the Contribution of Cover Crops and Manure to Nitrogen Nutrition in Corn and Wheat
items.summary: Despite available decision-support tools (DST), farmers still want to know how much nitrogen cover crops and manure actually supply under their own fields’ conditions. In this CEROM-led project, farmers across Quebec are co-designing and running strip trials in their own fields, testing five N rates after cover crops or manure. Results are used to directly evaluate and challenge DST against field-level responses. Early findings show a measurable N contribution from cover crops, informing real fertilizer decisions. To learn more, read here .

items.title: Data-Driven Sustainability: McGill University Launches Quebec’s First OFPE Network
items.summary: McGill University is launching Quebec's first On-Farm Precision Experimentation (OFPE) network. Over three years, 80 farms will lead their own trials to optimize nutrient management, soil cover, pesticide use, and biodiversity, aligned with the goals of the Plan d'agriculture durable . By merging academic rigor with real-world production, the network aims to scale precision agriculture across Eastern Canada through high-resolution, farm-specific data. To learn more.

items.title: 532 Trials and Counting: From the Field to the Zone
items.summary: The DIFM project automates site-specific data generation to help farmers optimize decisions. Since 2022, over 40 trials have been conducted in Quebec across inputs such as nitrogen, seeding rate, biostimulants, fungicides, and cover crops, bringing the global total to over 532. Building on this, CEROM is launching a project to test whether management zones derived from checkerboard trials remain reliable predictors of input response across seasons, an approach supported Adhikari et al. 2023 on multi-year yield stability and gross margin mapping. Click here to learn more .
items.publication: Adhikari K., Smith D.R., Hajda C. et al. (2023). Within-field yield stability and gross margin variations across corn fields and implications for precision conservation. Precision Agriculture.

items.title: A New Opportunity for Farmer-Centric OFE Publications
items.summary: Following the special section " Advances in On-Farm Agronomic Research and Participatory Learning " in Agronomy Journal, led by Peter Kyveryga, this community needed a new opportunity to publish farmer-centric OFE science. The co-chairs of this community worked with Frontiers in Agronomy to create one. The call for papers for the Research Topic " Farmer-Centric On-Farm Experimentation Enhanced by Digital Agronomy " is now open, with a submission deadline of October 10, 2026 . It welcomes contributions spanning agronomy, data science, and social science, from trial design and statistical methods to collaboration models and farmer-researcher partnerships. We will be featuring submitted and published papers here regularly as they come in. Learn more and submit your work .

items.title: The New York On-Farm Research Partnership puts farmers in the driver’s seat
items.summary: The New York On-Farm Research Partnership , led by the Nutrient Management Spear Program at Cornell University, pairs New York field crop producers with Cornell researchers, extension educators, and industry advisors to conduct wide-scale, statistically rigorous nutrient management field trials. By focusing on farmer-driven priorities, the partnership generates the large datasets needed to answer complex management questions efficiently. Results inform individual farm operations and are used to develop science-based guidance for both field-level and whole-farm nutrient management across New York. To learn more, read here .

items.title: New publication and OFE tool: SSEA for efficient farming decisions.
items.summary: The single-strip spatial evaluation approach (SSEA) web-based tool automates spatial analysis for single-strip on-farm trials, removing the need for statistical expertise. Developed with advisory feedback, the intuitive interface processes yield data and yield stability zone maps to generate result charts. These visuals provide site-specific interpretations of management changes across different zones. The tool empowers farmers to make data-driven decisions and promotes broader adoption of site-specific agricultural practices. Read journal and extension articles.
items.publication: Subhashree S.N., Goel R., Marcaida M. et al. (2025). Enhancing on‐farm research with a web‐based single‐strip spatial evaluation tool: Design, features, and applications. Agronomy Journal.

items.title: The Value and Power of Manure Projects: Improving manure management in NY
items.summary: While manure is a known driver of soil health and fertility, its specific nitrogen (N) fertilizer replacement value and ability to boost yield can be complex to quantify. The Value and Power of Manure project (2022-current) uses on-farm trials to measure the impact of different manure sources, application timings, and application methods on corn silage and grain yield. These findings help farmers optimize fertilizer offsets, improve farm economics, and enhance sustainability. To learn about our 2025 findings, read here .

items.title: Precision agriculture for on-farm research: Within-field yield stability zone management & remote sensing
items.summary: Commercial dairy and cash grain farms share yield data with the NMSP team to build multi-year, farm-specific Yield Stability Zone maps that separate consistent high-performing areas from variable or low-yielding ones. These maps support on-farm research to identify yield constraints and guide targeted input and management decisions. We are also evaluating remote sensing to estimate yield and generate zone maps. Together, these tools optimize fertility rates, improving profitability and environmental efficiency. Learn more: yield prediction , yield data processing , yield stability zones .

items.title: Tracking and enhancing farm sustainability using Dairy Sustainability Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
items.summary: This project provides dairy farms with science-based tools to track Nutrient Mass Balances, GHG inventories, and biodiversity. By monitoring nutrient imports and exports, participating New York farms have already reduced N and phosphorus imports by 20-30%, boosting profitability and sustainability. Farms are also demonstrating that milk can be produced with low GHG inventories. Confidential, benchmarked farm reports help producers identify specific management changes that improve efficiency and meet environmental goals while maintaining economic viability. Learn more .

items.title: New Open-Access Review: Advanced Data Analytics for OFE
items.summary: Tanaka, Colaço, Mieno, and Riley have published a comprehensive open-access review in Plant Production Science (Vol. 29, No. 2) covering the full landscape of data analytics for OFE . The paper surveys statistical approaches for spatially heterogeneous field data, machine learning methods for site-specific management, cross-site synthesis frameworks, and simulation-based tools for evaluating experimental designs. It also looks ahead at emerging opportunities, including causal ML, smartphone-based yield estimation for smallholder systems, and the potential role of large language models in supporting farmer-researcher communication. items.title: #OFE2021 Conference Papers Now Independently Searchable
items.summary: The 47 papers from the First International Conference on Farmer-centric On-Farm Experimentation (#OFE2021, Montpellier, October 2021) have been published as independent, peer-reviewed, citable records in the Cornell eCommons repository. Each paper is now discoverable through scientific search engines like Google Scholar, giving this body of work the visibility it deserves. The collection covers the four core OFE themes from the conference: people and processes, value creation, data and analytics, and policy linkages. For those who missed the original proceedings, the full multimedia document gathering all 190 contributions, including papers, video presentations, and policy outputs, remains freely available as well. Visit the new collection (47 independent papers) here . And rthe original proceedings (PDF) here .

items.title: Talking Soil: A Podcast on Science, Soil Health, and the People Who Manage Land
items.summary: Soil health depends on both biology and human decision-making, and making science and practice work together is precisely the challenge OFE seeks to address. This ConnectSci podcast with soil scientists Lisa Lobry de Bruyn and Oliver Knox explores what it means to truly know your soil. A companion book, Talking Soil , is forthcoming from CSIRO Publishing in early 2027. Listen to the podcast here .

items.title: The Value of Soil Testing for Long-Term Farm Decision-Making
items.summary: Soil testing is often used for short-term decisions, but a longer-term vision is gaining ground. An MLA article makes the case for soil testing as a foundation for stocking rate decisions, and findings from the Soil CRC Rural Landholder Survey show that while farmers recognize its importance, implementation remains limited, often due to availability constraints. Understanding what farmers actually do and why is essential context for designing relevant OFE. Read the MLA article here .

items.title: Visualising Australasia's Soils: Open Soil Data for Better On-Farm Decisions
items.summary: Visualising Australasia's Soils (VAS) is a Soil CRC portal bringing together public and private soil data from across Australia and New Zealand under FAIR principles. Its explicit goal of improving on-farm decision making through long-term trends and benchmarking makes it a directly relevant resource for OFE practitioners. Explore the project here or go directly to the data portal here .

items.title: Learning from Farmers Who Know Their Soil: Soils for Life
items.summary: As soils are diverse then understanding your soil requires the landholder to become the local expert. Placing your trust in your own senses and intellect to get to know your soil. Soils for Life has built from its tradition and shares the stories of Australia’s leading farmers. They would like to inspire others to “move from curiosity to confidence”. To do this they have produced case studies and practice guides on monitoring soil health . To learn more, go to their website .

items.title: Empower-OFE: Empowering Farmer-centric Agricultural Transformation
items.summary: For the longest time, farmers in the global south have been peripheral to agricultural innovation processes, relegated to mere recipients of technologies generated by external actors. Empower-OFE is a key flagship program of the African Plant Nutrition Institute (APNI) dedicated towards transforming African agricultural landscapes through farmer-centric approaches, models and methods. Find out more about what we are doing to empower farmers to be innovative agents of change here .

items.title: Reframing Innovation in African Agriculture: Why OFE is the game-changer
items.summary: Many in the scientific community, particularly in Africa, conflate On-Farm Experimentation (OFE) with On-Farm Research (OFR). They fail to recognize the nuances that make farmer-led OFE stand-out in terms of shifting paradigms from researcher-led to farmer-led, entrenching co-creation and co-learning, enhancing relevance of agricultural technologies to farmers and accelerating scaling of relevant technologies. Find out more about these issues from excerpts of a peer-reviewed review article by APNI scientists and collaborators.

items.title: From the Ground Up: How Farmers are Shaping the Future of Agriculture in Kenya
items.summary: In August 2025, APNI operationalized a fully-fledged farmer-led on-farm experimentation process (OFE 2.0), which will form part of the building blocks of a self-sustaining OFE service model in Kenya. The initiative commenced with stakeholder engagement meetings held on 11-22 August 2025 in western and eastern Kenya. An expanded network of > 200 OFE farmers who are experimenting with different technologies is now in place. Read more about this initiative here .

items.title: Driving Farmer-Centered Agricultural Transformation in Ghana
items.summary: The Nutrient-Catalyzed Agricultural Transformation (NUTCAT) Project, led by the African Plant Nutrition Institute in collaboration with the CSIR – Savanna Agricultural Research Institute (SARI) and supported by Ghana’s Ministry of Food and Agriculture, was implemented from 2022 -2024 to address the problems of low cereal productivity in Ghana’s Northern and Middle Belt regions. At the core of this initiative was OFE, which ensured innovations generated were locally relevant and adoptable. Watch this video for more information on how OFE is transforming cereal systems in Ghana.

items.title: OFE improves nutrient management decision-making for East and West African Farmers
items.summary: A recently published peer-reviewed paper shows the integral role of OFE in enhancing co-learning and improving yield and income outcomes in African smallholder farmer settings. This comparative study drawing on data from Kenya, Tanzania and Côte d’ Ivoire used a mixed methodology approach to evaluate farmer learning, nutrient management decision-making, and outcomes from their involvement with OFE under auspices of the NUTCAT project. You can find the open-source article here .

items.title: Inspiring from Other Sectors: What Medical Case Reporting Can Teach OFE
items.summary: Replace " clinical case report " with " on-farm experiment " and this review maps almost directly onto OFE: detecting novelties, generating hypotheses, in-depth narrative understanding, and value where controlled trials are impossible. The limitations will also sound familiar. Though Pearl's work on causal inference ( The Book of Why ) would now challenge the claim that case reports cannot establish cause-effect relationships. See a post on this here and the full paper here .
items.publication: Nissen T., Wynn R. (2014). The clinical case report: a review of its merits and limitations. BMC Research Notes.

items.title: 38 Years of Farmer-Led Research: The Practical Farmers of Iowa Cooperators' Program
items.summary: Since 1987, over 240 farmers have designed and led nearly 1,300 trials through the Practical Farmers of Iowa Cooperators' Program, with farmers setting the research goals and priorities from the start. In 2025 alone, 107 farmers led 185 trials. This is farmer-centric OFE at scale, and arguably the best-documented long-running program of its kind anywhere in the world. Explore the trial reports here .

items.title: Who Decides Which Trials Go on Your Farm? The AHDB Farmer Marketplace
items.summary: The AHDB Farmer Marketplace flips the traditional research model: researchers pitch their on-farm research opportunities, and participating farmers retain full power to opt in or out, deciding which trials happen on their land. It is one of the clearest governance examples of farmer agency in OFE, and a model worth knowing about for anyone thinking about how to structure farmer-scientist partnerships. Learn more here .

items.title: £8 Return for Every £1 Invested: The Innovative Farmers Field Labs
items.summary: The UK's Innovative Farmers program supported a network of around 185 field labs, each receiving up to £10,000, with an estimated direct benefit of £8 per £1 invested. Beyond the numbers, it demonstrated that farmer-led research can be both scientifically credible and economically compelling. The program concluded in 2022, but its results remain a strong reference for making the case that investing in farmer-centric OFE can pay off. Learn more here .

items.title: Farmer-Led, Scientist-Supported: The Farmers DataLab at Cornell
items.summary: Farmers set the questions, scientists quantify the effects. That is the philosophy behind the Farmers DataLab at Cornell, and this article captures what becomes possible when farmers and scientists genuinely collaborate. Graduate student Katie Rohrbaugh puts it simply: "Farmers know their land better than a scientist ever could... it's a skill-share." A good read for anyone in the OFE community, and a useful resource to share with colleagues who are new to the concept. Read the full article here .
